author: 在原元方
translation: With spring's arrival,
will the white snow on the branches be seen as flowers—
while the bush warbler sings?

author: 凡河内躬恒
translation: The darkness of a spring night is no mystery:
the plum blossoms cannot be seen,
but can their fragrance be hidden?

author: 紀友則
translation: In the gentle light
of a peaceful spring day,
why do the blossoms fall with such restless hearts?

author: 小野小町
translation: The flowers' colors have faded
as I spent my days in idle thought
watching the long rains fall.

author: 清原深養父
translation: Though it was still early evening,
the summer night has already dawned—
where among the clouds does the moon now rest?

author: よみ人しらず
translation: When I breathe the scent
of orange blossoms that wait for May,
it is the fragrance from a loved one's sleeve long ago.

author: 紀秋岑
translation: Has the one I long for
gone into the summer mountains?
The cuckoo calls out, pouring forth its voice.

author: 藤原敏行
translation: Autumn has come, though it cannot yet be clearly seen;
only the sound of the wind makes me realize it.

author: 文屋朝康
translation: In the autumn fields,
where wind blows through the white dew,
unstrung jewels scatter everywhere.

author: 在原業平朝臣
translation: Even in the age of the gods,
none had heard of the Tatsuta River
binding its waters in crimson.

author: よみ人しらず
translation: When I hear a stag
calling as it treads through fallen leaves
deep in the mountain,
autumn feels sorrowful.

author: 坂上是則
translation: White snow seems to be piling
on Mount Yoshino;
the old capital grows ever colder.

author: 源宗于朝臣
translation: A mountain village
feels lonelier still in winter,
when people and grasses alike have withered away.

author: 清原深養父
translation: Though it is winter,
flowers scatter down from the sky—
perhaps beyond the clouds it is already spring.

author: 紀友則
translation: When snow falls,
the grasses and trees hidden through winter
bloom with flowers
no spring has taught them to know.
